citations.quote: The submitted one pivotal study (#022) (to demonstrate the efficacy of rufinamide as adjunctive therapy in patients with inadequately controlled seizures associated with LGS) was a multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized, parallel-group study.

design.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial with a 28-day Baseline Phase followed by an 84-day (12-week) Double-blind Phase during which BANZEL or placebo was added to 1 to 3 concomitant stable-dose AEDs; target dose approximately 45 mg/kg/day

citations.quote: Study#022 was a multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized, parallel-group study of rufinamide as adjunctive therapy in patients with inadequately controlled seizures associated with LGS. population.text: Male or female patients 4 to 30 years of age with inadequately controlled seizures associated with LGS (including atypical absence seizures and drop attacks) treated with 1 to 3 concomitant fixed-dose AEDs

citations.quote: Male or female patients (between 4 and 30 years of age) were included if they had a diagnosis of inadequately controlled seizures associated with LGS (including both atypical absence seizures and drop attacks) and were being treated with one to three concomitant fixed-dose antiepileptic drugs (AEDs).

endpoint.text: Three co-primary efficacy variables: percent change in total seizure frequency per 28 days, percent change in tonic-atonic (drop attack) seizure frequency per 28 days, and seizure severity from the Parent/Guardian Global Evaluation

key_safety.text: In the pediatric LGS/adjunctive population the most common adverse reactions (>=3%, higher than placebo) included somnolence (17% vs 9%), vomiting (17% vs 7%), and headache (16% vs 8%); in adults the most common were headache (27% vs 26%), dizziness (19% vs 12%), and fatigue (16% vs 10%). Somnolence was reported in 24.3% of BANZEL-treated patients vs 12.5% of placebo patients. BANZEL also shortens the QT interval (up to 20 msec).

summary.text: NDA 21-911 for rufinamide was submitted November 17, 2005; an Approvable letter was issued September 15, 2006 and the sponsor's complete response was submitted February 29, 2008, leading to approval of the Lennox-Gastaut syndrome indication, which carries an orphan drug designation. A REMS with a Medication Guide was required.
